titleEn: It's Okay to Cry on Grandma's Lap!

pages.text: "I want to carry it myself!" Dingding lifted a rice bundle with both hands on the bank. Dingding wanted to carry it to the yard, just like Mom, who worked several paddies on her own. The bundle was as tall as Dingding and hid half their face.
One step, then another. A stone caught Dingding's toe. Down went Dingding and the bundle! Their knee stung, and the bundle rolled along the bank.
Mom called from the higher paddy, "Are you all right?" Dingding jumped up and covered their knee. "It doesn't hurt! Not at all!" But their throat felt tight, and their eyes kept growing hot.
Dingding limped into the yard. Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, sat in the doorway sorting rice ears. She saw Dingding's knee and beckoned. "Come here."
"Grandma, it doesn't hurt. Only babies cry." Grandma patted her lap. "Pretending it doesn't hurt makes it hurt more. You can cry here." Her lap was broad and warm.
Dingding buried their face in Grandma's lap. The tears they had held back burst out. "Waaah! My knee hurts!" Grandma stroked their back. "Yes. It's Okay to Cry on Grandma's Lap!"

When the crying was over, Dingding's tight throat felt clear. Dingding peeked up, and Grandma wiped the tears with the edge of her clothes. Sniffling, Dingding repeated, "It's Okay to Cry on Grandma's Lap!"
Mom came into the yard holding the fallen bundle. "I brought yours back." Dingding sniffed its sunny smell. "My knee hurts less now!" Their eyes curved into little half-moons.

A few days later, Dingding bumped a foot on the threshold and went straight to Grandma's lap. "One, point to the hurt and say it hurts! Two, cry if tears come! Three, go to Grandma's lap!" "Grandma, it hurts."

Grandma sat Dingding on her lap and hugged them tightly. "Saying it hurts is the bravest thing to do." After crying, the hurt felt lighter. Dingding rubbed their face against Grandma's lap. "It's Okay to Cry on Grandma's Lap!"
